so to a screen reader.

StretchedLink.description:
A transparent link stretched over its positioned container (a row; a Card
draws its own with `onOpen`), so a click anywhere opens the view the
container summarises. It's a link to a screen reader, as it moves to another
view rather than acting. A control in the container raises itself above it
and stays a sibling, never nested. The focus ring follows the container's
corners, just inside the edge; `className` can round it where they don't (a
list's first and last rows). `data-stretched-link` lets the container style
itself while it has focus.

Dialog.description:
A modal dialog: title, optional description and close button, a recessed
body, an optional footnote, and a footer of actions. Focus moves in and
stays inside while it's open, the page behind is inert, and focus returns to
the opener on close. Escape, the close button, Cancel and a click on the
backdrop all call `onClose`.

Render it inside a DialogRoot, which opens it and plays its leave animation.

pulse.description:
A pulse whose shape says what it marks: `calm`, a slow shallow breath, for
a steady state (connected); `busy`, a quick deep throb, for work under way
(a scan); `live`, one quicker, deeper breath, for data streaming in. Live
runs once: give the dot a new `key` on each update, as `LiveBadge` does,
so it breathes in step with the numbers, and set `--live-elapsed` to the
update's age so one that mounts between updates picks up in step. With no
update for 3s it fades to dim, as the data has stalled.

whose words stay quiet (online), or `accent` for work under way (a scan).

in the content area. A status region, so the line is announced.

Banner.description:
A message above a page: icon, title, a line under it, then Dismiss and
Retry on the right. Dismiss hides this title until it changes or the banner
unmounts, so a poll that fails the same way again doesn't bring it back; a
caller renders it only while there's an error, which is what resets it.

description.description: One short line under the title: how old what's on screen is, or what happens next.

onRetry.description: Shows Retry, busy until the returned promise settles.

title.description: What happened. Dismiss hides the banner until this changes.

variant.description: `error`, a failure, shown until it clears: a red wash, and a red Dismiss.

whenToUse: A failure above a page: a load, scan or action that didn’t work.

whenNotToUse: A page loaded with nothing to show: use `EmptyState`.

toHandle: A title that says what failed: “Couldn’t scan for devices”.

DataListStack.description:

with `--divider-space` either side of it. The hairline runs end to end, so place
the stack flush to the card's sides (`CardBody layout="flush"`); each
group carries the side inset itself.

Card.description:
The panel surface, clipped to its rounded corners. Build it from a
CardHeader, a CardBody and an optional CardFooter, or lay out your own
content in an element of your own inside it. With `onOpen` the whole card
is a link; a control inside it raises itself above the link (`relative z-2`).

propsNotInFigma.as: The HTML element: it looks the same.

as.description:
`section` is named by its CardHeader's title, so give it one.
`div` or `li` for a card with no header, such as a card in a list.

children.description: A CardHeader, a CardBody and an optional CardFooter, or your own content.

className.description: Its place in a layout: a width (`max-w-[320px]`) or a grid span (`col-span-2`).

linkLabel.description:
What a screen reader says for the card's link, which has no visible text,
when its CardHeader's title isn't enough: what the card shows, then where
it goes ("Usage: 3.2 GB today. Open Usage."). A card with no CardHeader needs it.

onOpen.description: Opens the view the card summarises: the whole card is its link, and its header ends in a caret.

whenNotToUse: An error about the whole page: use `Banner`.

otherExports.PortalProvider: Sets where the library's dialogs inside it portal to.
otherExports.STATUS_TEXT:
The status text colours (green, amber, red), keyed as recipes name their
status axis: `status: STATUS_TEXT`, or `{ positive: STATUS_TEXT.positive, … }`
for a subset.
otherExports.cn:
Join class names, skipping falsy ones, and let later Tailwind utilities win
over earlier ones that set the same thing: `cn('px-12', className)` with
`className="px-8"` gives `px-8`. Use it wherever a component merges its own
classes with a `className` from outside; plain joins can use `cx`.
otherExports.focusCardLink:
Moves focus to the link of the openable card holding `element`: for a
control in it that's about to unmount, so focus stays in the card instead
of falling back to the page.
otherExports.moveFocusBetweenRows:
A list's `onKeyDown`: Up and Down move focus to the next or previous row's
control, and Home and End to the first or last. Each row stays its own Tab
stop, so the arrows are a shortcut on top of Tab. Not `useRovingFocus`: a
roving tabindex suits a toolbar or the nav rail, and would hide all but one
row of a plain list from Tab and from a screen reader's list.
otherExports.useCountUp:
Eases a displayed number toward `target` each animation frame, so the value
visibly counts up or down instead of snapping. It snaps under reduced motion
(the global rule stops only CSS animations, not this one), and to or from a
value that isn't finite, which no ease could reach.
otherExports.useLatestRef:
A ref that always holds the latest `value`, for callbacks that must read
fresh props without re-subscribing. Read only from an effect? Use React's
`useEffectEvent` instead; this is for code that runs outside effects too.

The ref is written in a layout effect rather than during render, so a render
React throws away never leaks into it. Read it only outside render.
otherExports.usePresence:
Whether an element that animates out should still be mounted.

Rendering `{isActive && <X />}` drops the element the moment `isActive` turns
false, so a leave animation never gets to play. Render `<X />` while this
returns true instead, and style it as leaving while `isActive` is false: it
mounts as soon as `isActive` turns true and unmounts `exitMs` after it turns
false, which should match the length of the leave animation. Turning active
again before then cancels the unmount.
otherExports.useRovingFocus:
Makes a group of items one Tab stop (a roving tabindex): the arrow keys move
between them, and Home and End jump to the ends. Leaving the group puts the
stop back on the `currentSelector` item. It sets the items' `tabIndex`, so they
mustn't set their own.

Not Base UI's Toolbar, its only public roving focus: it makes the group a
`toolbar`, and its items throw outside one, but NavItem also stands alone.
